A factory function like createStation(name, x, y, dwellTicks) has these advantages over new Station(...):

No new keyword required

Calling createStation(...) is just a function call — no risk of forgetting new and silently getting undefined or corrupting the global scope.
Flexible return type

The factory can decide what to return — a plain object, a class instance, a frozen object, or even a different subtype based on input (e.g., a terminus station vs. a passing station), without changing the call site.
Easier to compose and test

A plain object returned from a factory has no prototype chain to worry about. Mocking in tests is trivial — just pass in a literal { name, x, y, dwellTicks }.
Encapsulation without classes

You can close over private state using variables in the factory's scope, without needing #privateField syntax.
Consistent with how your codebase works

Your existing objects (Flyover, Intersection) are constructed with new, but station data is essentially a value object — it holds data, not behavior. A factory returning a plain object is idiomatic for that.
Practical example in your context:


// Factory — returns a plain data objectfunction createStation(name, x, y, dwellTicks, stopOnReturn = true) {  return { name, x, y, dwellTicks, stopOnReturn, distanceFromStart: null }}// vs class — adds prototype overhead for a pure data recordclass Station {  constructor(name, x, y, dwellTicks, stopOnReturn = true) { ... }}
For a station, which is just a data record attached to a route, the factory is the right choice — it produces plain, serializable objects with no overhead.

That error means your droplet is reaching GitHub, but GitHub does not trust the SSH key from that server yet.

Run these on the droplet as the same user doing git clone (you said root):

1. Create an SSH key (if you do not already have one)
```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "droplet-deploy"
```
Press Enter for defaults.

2. Start ssh-agent and load key
```bash
eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

3. Copy public key
```bash
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
```

4. Add this key to GitHub
- Go to your repo on GitHub
- Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key
- Paste the key
- Enable read access (or write if needed)

5. Trust GitHub host key
```bash
ssh-keyscan github.com >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts
chmod 700 ~/.ssh
chmod 600 ~/.ssh/known_hosts
```

6. Test SSH auth
```bash
ssh -T git@github.com
```
You should see a success message like “Hi username...”.

7. Clone again
```bash
git clone git@github.com:OWNER/REPO.git
```

If it still fails, run this and share output:
```bash
ssh -vT git@github.com
```

Quick fallback option:
Use HTTPS clone instead of SSH:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.git
```
For private repos, use a GitHub Personal Access Token when prompted for password.









Yes. In your current setup, you have two sound paths and each has different options:

File-based playback (HTML Audio)
Synthesized playback (Web Audio API)
How they are defined:

Audio manager construction is in audioManager.js.
Core implementation is in utility.js:170.
1. Global AudioManager options (at creation time)



laneOccupancy is the runtime map that tracks which train is currently occupying each grid cell, per lane.

How it is structured:
1. It is initialized as a Map in `Intersections.js:12`.
2. Top-level key is a cell key string from row,col via `Intersections.js:16`.
3. Value is another Map for lanes at that cell:
- lane number -> train number

So conceptually:
- cell 10,20 -> { lane 0: train 2, lane 1: train 5 }

How it is used in updateIntersection:
1. Cell bounds and special-cell guard run first in `Intersections.js:106`.
2. It fetches per-cell lane map:
- occupancyByLane = laneOccupancy.get(cellKey) at `Intersections.js:116`
3. If trainNumber is null/undefined, it means clear occupancy for that lane:
- delete lane entry
- remove cell entry if no lanes remain
- this is in `Intersections.js:118-126`
4. If a train is entering:
- it checks current train on same lane
- if same lane already has a different train, collision logic runs
- if allowedTrainsByCell says both are allowed at that cell, collision is skipped
- collision branch is in `Intersections.js:130-152`
5. If no conflict:
- it sets lane -> train in the per-cell map
- stores map back to laneOccupancy
- in `Intersections.js:153-155`

Why per-lane matters:
1. Two trains can be in same cell without collision if they are on different lanes (depends on how caller passes lane).
2. Collision check is lane-specific, not just cell-specific.

When it gets cleared:
1. Flyover/station update clears occupancy for that cell in:
- `Intersections.js:163`
- `Intersections.js:171`
2. removeTrain walks all laneOccupancy entries and removes that train from every lane in `Intersections.js:175-187`.

In short:
- laneOccupancy is the live occupancy state used for immediate collision detection.
- intersections grid stores static cell type state like Flyover/Station.
- laneOccupancy is dynamic, updated every movement step.

- For the tutorial video source around `index.html:297`, avoid full download before user opens it.

5. Remove unused large assets from deploy output.
- You appear to have some large files not currently referenced; keep them out of shipped build.

6. Enable compression at server level.
- Gzip/Brotli for js/css/html and cache headers significantly improve repeat loads.

Fastest practical target:
- You can likely reduce first interactive wait from around 20+ MB down to roughly 6 to 10 MB by combining steps 1 to 4.

Made changes.

After you change code, you have 2 ways to work:

1. One-time bundle build
- Run: npm run build
- This creates/updates the bundle once in dist.
- If you edit code again, it will NOT rebuild automatically until you run build again.

2. Auto rebuild while developing
- Run: npm run dev (or npm run watch)
- This watches your files and rebuilds bundle.js automatically on every save.

About your current URL (http://127.0.0.1:5500/index.html):
- Yes, that URL can still work for the original app source from your project root.
- But that path is not the esbuild served output.
- For bundled output, use the esbuild dev server URL:
  - http://127.0.0.1:5173/

So in practice:
- Keep using 5500 if you want the old direct-source run style.
- Use 5173 if you want the bundled/watch workflow (recommended with esbuild).

I now have a folder in root folder called train_operations in Digital Ocean droplet. 
I also have an nginx file somewhere there which successfully serves my other web site. 
How do I add a server block in nginx file so that this (train_operations) web site is also served.

Use a second Nginx server block for a new domain/subdomain, pointing to your new static folder.

1. Create a site config file
   sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/train_operations

2. Paste this block (edit domain and root path)
   
   server {
       listen 80;
       listen [::]:80;

       server_name trains.yourdomain.com;
       root /root/train_operations;
       index index.html;

       location / {
           try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
       }

       location ~* \.(css|js|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|svg|ico|webp)$ {
           expires 7d;
           add_header Cache-Control "public";
       }
   }

3. Enable the site
   sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/train_operations /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/

When I ran 'sudo systemctl reload nginx' I get the error nginx service is not running!

That means Nginx is installed but currently stopped, so reload cannot work until it starts.

Run these in order on the droplet:

1. Validate config first
sudo nginx -t

2. Check why service is down
sudo systemctl status nginx --no-pager -l

3. Try starting it
sudo systemctl start nginx

4. If start succeeds, enable and reload
sudo systemctl enable nginx
sudo systemctl reload nginx

If step 3 fails, get exact error details:
sudo journalctl -u nginx -n 100 --no-pager

Most common causes:

1. Bad server block syntax
Fix the line reported by nginx -t, then run:
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl start nginx

2. Port 80/443 already used by another service (often Apache)
Check:
sudo ss -ltnp | findstr ":80 :443"
If Apache is using it:
sudo systemctl stop apache2
sudo systemctl disable apache2
sudo systemctl start nginx

3. Wrong file permissions when serving from /root
Nginx (www-data) often cannot read under /root. Move site to /var/www/train_operations and point root there.

If you paste output from nginx -t and systemctl status nginx, I can tell you the exact fix immediately.

A 500 from Nginx usually means a config/runtime error, not DNS. The fastest path is: read the exact error line, then apply the likely static-site fix.

Run these on the droplet:

1. Validate Nginx config
   sudo nginx -t

2. Read recent Nginx errors
   sudo tail -n 120 /var/log/nginx/error.log

3. Check service status
   sudo systemctl status nginx --no-pager -l

Most likely fix for your setup

If this is a static site, use a clean server block like this (no php, no proxy lines):

server {
    listen 80;
    listen [::]:80;
    server_name playtraingame.com [www.playtraingame.com](http://www.playtraingame.com);

    root /var/www/train_operations;
    index index.html;

    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
    }
}

Then move files out of /root and set permissions:

1. Create web root
   sudo mkdir -p /var/www/train_operations

2. Copy site files
   sudo cp -r /root/train_operations/* /var/www/train_operations/

3. Set ownership and permissions
   sudo chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/train_operations
   sudo find /var/www/train_operations -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \;
   sudo find /var/www/train_operations -type f -exec chmod 644 {} \;

4. Test and reload
   sudo nginx -t
   sudo systemctl reload nginx

Why this usually fixes it:
1. Serving from /root often breaks access/security context.
2. A reused config from another app may still contain php-fpm or proxy directives that can trigger 500.
3. SPA fallback works only if `index.html` exists in the configured root.

If you paste:
1. your server block
2. last 30 lines from /var/log/nginx/error.log

I can pinpoint the exact broken line and give you the one-line fix.


2. Set ownership and permissions
```bash
sudo chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/train_operations
sudo find /var/www/train_operations -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \;
sudo find /var/www/train_operations -type f -exec chmod 644 {} \;
```

3. Update your Nginx server block root to:
```nginx
root /var/www/train_operations;
index index.html;
location / {
    try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
}
```

4. Test and reload
```bash
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

5. If it still fails, check exact error lines
```bash
sudo tail -n 80 /var/log/nginx/error.log
```

Yes, there is one important change still needed, and one likely runtime check.

1. Change the HTTP block so both hostnames redirect to HTTPS.
Right now only riversidebridgeclub.com is handled on port 80, while www can fall through to 404.

2. Keep the HTTPS proxy block as-is for both names.

Use this full config for that site:

```nginx
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name riversidebridgeclub.com www.riversidebridgeclub.com;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade;
    }

    ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/riversidebridgeclub.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/riversidebridgeclub.com/privkey.pem;
    include /etc/letsencrypt/options-ssl-nginx.conf;
    ssl_dhparam /etc/letsencrypt/ssl-dhparams.pem;
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name riversidebridgeclub.com www.riversidebridgeclub.com;
    return 301 https://riversidebridgeclub.com$request_uri;
}
```

Then run:

```bash
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

```bash
sudo ss -ltnp | grep :3000
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

If nothing is listening on 3000, this domain cannot work until your Node app is started (pm2/systemd/manual).

1. Install PM2

   pm2 startup
   Follow the one command PM2 prints, then run:

   pm2 list
   pm2 logs riverside --lines 100

Two separate things were wrong:

1. Scope bug in your zoom fix  
At `utility.js:684`, the previous change used `gameZoomLevel` inside `utility.js`, but `gameZoomLevel` is declared in `script.js:183` (module-local there).  
So `utility.js` should not depend on that variable directly.

2. Mixed coordinate spaces in demo  
In `demo.js:184` and `demo.js:218`, values from `getBoundingClientRect()` (already client coordinates) were being fed into the canvas-to-client converter, which expects canvas coordinates. That double-conversion breaks positions when zoom is not 1.

There was also a build/runtime mismatch:
- The page loads dist/bundle.js, so changing source files alone does nothing until rebuilding.

What I changed:
- Updated canvas conversion to use actual rendered scale (`rect.width / canvas.width`) in `utility.js:678`, which naturally handles zoom and avoids `gameZoomLevel`.
- Fixed demo start/end animation points to use client-space values directly in `demo.js:184` and `demo.js:218`.
- Rebuilt with `npm.cmd run build` so `bundle.js` is updated.
